A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original active-learning experiments on ColorSwap, MS-COCO, and DataComp, including learning curves, modality-selection ablations, and supplementary model comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds runtime measurements, robustness studies, alignment-quality results, and an adapted BADGE comparison.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 are unchanged, including modality selection, coreset construction, margin-based acquisition, and model updates. Distance caching, emphasized in v2 Section 4.1, was already described in v1 Appendix A, Remark 1. The added controlled variants do not replace the proposed method.

E1.justification: The three datasets and principal tasks are retained. v2 adds a distinct missing-data scenario on ColorSwap: half the images are removed while all captions remain, leaving unmatched captions (Section 6, Figure 4 right). This extends input conditions within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates Rand, Coreset, and Uncertainty. v2 additionally evaluates an adapted BADGE baseline on ColorSwap with CLIP-B32 (Appendix C.4, Figure 9 right), retaining the original comparators. BADGE's earlier citation did not constitute an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary evaluation procedures: pseudo-labeling accuracy and GroupMatch metrics, runtime measurements over 512–4096 candidates, image-only querying in the missing-image experiment, and cosine-distance controls. Appendix C.2 compares DataComp buffers of 1024 and 2048 while selecting 25%, coupling training batch sizes of 256 and 512. Existing main protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6 and Appendices C.2–C.3 add direct runtime-scaling measurements and tests of missing-image robustness, streaming-buffer sensitivity, and distance-metric sensitivity. These substantially extend the earlier modality-selection, coreset-size, margin-score, and t-SNE analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over four random runs and plot shading represents two-thirds of a standard deviation. v2 extends the existing uncertainty-reporting practice to additional results without introducing new run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained learning curves and Tables 2–3 are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results in Figures 4 and 9 and Tables 4 and 8. For example, Table 4 reports pseudo-labeling accuracy of 80.39±0.71 and GroupMatch of 87.14±0.22 for Ours, versus 79.81±0.73 and 86.57±0.29 for Random. Additional findings cover runtime, missing images, buffer size, cosine distance, and BADGE.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 and Appendix A incorporate caching already described in v1 Remark 1. The per-round bound changes from O(B_C|D_t||S_{t-1}|) to O((B_C+|S_{t-1}|)|D_t|), and the total bound from O(T^2 B B_C|D|) to O(T(B_C+TB)|D|). The proof is correspondingly refined, and v2 explicitly states T=O(1) and B_C much smaller than |D| when discussing linear scaling.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: active acquisition of unaligned multimodal pairings, a modality-aware uncertainty/diversity algorithm, linear acquisition scaling, pool and streaming applicability, and annotation savings up to 40%.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of redundant uncertainty-only selections and hypothesizes that large gradient-embedding dimensions weaken adapted BADGE. It interprets the new robustness results and expands the earlier generative-model future-work statement into an explicit limitation: acquisition and uncertainty estimation would require non-trivial modifications.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies default streaming buffers of 1024 for MS-COCO and 2048 for DataComp, plus acquisition sizes of 70, 256, and 512 across the three datasets. Appendix C.4 describes BADGE's random-modality, classification-loss adaptation. These disclosures supplement unchanged original hyperparameter tables.

R1.justification: v2 adds distinctions from mismatched-pair repair by Han et al. (2024) and encoder alignment by Kimura et al. (2025), plus citations to Zhang and Chaudhuri (2014) and Zhu et al. (2026). Appendix C.4 further positions the method against BADGE. Publication updates to existing references do not represent new cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction and related-work rewrites, corrects the Section 4.1 heading, and expands method explanations and the conclusion. Supplementary results move from Appendix B.3 to C.1, followed by new subsections. The principal section sequence and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and 8 and Figure 9. Figure 4 combines the earlier Figure 5 t-SNE visualization with new runtime and missing-data panels; the earlier coreset-sensitivity Figure 4 becomes Figure 5. Retained plots are resized or repositioned, with some legend adjustments, while the overall visual format remains consistent.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through runtime measurements, the BADGE comparison, and additional robustness checks, while clarifying acquisition settings, the existing caching analysis, and applicability limits. The gains are useful but bounded: the missing-data test permits only image queries with valid counterparts, and the buffer study also changes training batch size. These additions modestly improve validation and clarity without resolving broader robustness questions.
